name: crypto-hmac256
algorithm: std HMAC-SHA256 (RFC 2104) of every 64-byte message of splitmix64 bytes under a 32-byte key, reps passes with the key's first byte updated per pass (mk/crypto-hmac256.mk).

skip.c: no std crypto: C has no standard HMAC
skip.rust: no std crypto: Rust std has no HMAC; no crate stands in

notes: Work per step: one HMAC-SHA256 of one 64-byte message under the 32-byte key, the pads absorbed per message on every side (5 SHA-256 compressions). Mk crypto.Hmac256 (one shot), Zig HmacSha256.create (one shot), Go hmac.New + Write + Sum (Go has no one-shot function; New hashes the key's pads each time, as the others). Messages per second = mib * 16384 * reps / median.
Go: crypto/sha256 uses the SHA extensions (SHA-NI) on amd64 when the CPU has them; Mk and Zig (at -mcpu=x86_64_v2) are scalar.

Checksums: every column printed the same value at the quick and the publish args in `go run ./tools/bench verify` and `verify -publish-size` (mk built from the tree, Zig 0.17.0, Go 1.27.3) on the owner's machine, 2026-11-07 (std-crypto session 1). Not published: no number here is a measurement.
